findings.title: Rollback export asserts at-rest 'encrypted' control that §5 explicitly defers
findings.detail: §5 ADR.01.05.98ff records at-rest encryption + key-management + rotation as DEFERRED to the data-protection ADR (BRD.01.08.daeb), with the interim compensating control being least-privilege grant + managed-tier volume encryption. §7's rollback step (2) states the PII-column export 'inherits the access/at-rest controls (encrypted, least-privilege, secure-deleted; params owned by BRD.01.08.daeb)'. The word 'encrypted' here asserts an at-rest export control whose algorithm/key-management this ADR has not decided and explicitly punts. It correctly delegates params to the sibling ADR, and managed-tier volume encryption plausibly covers the export media at rest, so this is a wording-level coupling, not an uncovered control — but the export of a may-contain-PII column out of the managed store is precisely the moment the deferred at-rest control becomes load-bearing, and an auditor reading §5 alone would not know the export is in scope of the sibling decision.
findings.recommendation: Make the export's at-rest dependency explicit: state that the rollback export of the PII column is gated on the data-protection ADR (BRD.01.08.daeb) at-rest controls being in place, or that the interim managed-tier volume encryption is the operative at-rest control for the export until then. Keeps §7 and §5 consistent on what 'encrypted' means pre-sibling-ADR.
